RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-5FADD4BBDE-47544
Notice Date: August 14, 2026
Requested Service: Total hip arthroplasty, CPT 27130
Treating Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 14, 2026. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am requesting that Aetna reverse this determination based on the clinical record summarized below, which I believe satisfies the medical-necessity criteria that Aetna itself has published for hip arthroplasty.

1. Governing policy

The document identified as governing this procedure is Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0287, "Hip Arthroplasty" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/200_299/0287.html). Aetna's own "PCFX Hip Arthroplasty Precertification Information Request Form" (form GR-69581-2) directs providers to "review Clinical Policy Bulletin #287: Hip Arthroplasty" before submitting a request for this exact procedure. I could not confirm the specific "last reviewed" or effective date of the Bulletin from the publicly posted page, so I am asking Aetna to identify and produce the exact version and effective date of CPB 0287 that was applied to this request, along with any internal review criteria used, so that the record is complete.

2. Radiographic findings

CPB 0287 states that medical necessity for total hip arthroplasty requires "Radiographic evidence of either of the following: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) with stage II or III disease; or Moderate/severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint (Tonnis grade 2 or 3...)."

Aetna's own precertification form for this procedure lists as a qualifying finding: "Moderate/Severe Osteoarthritis or Rheumatoid arthritis (shown on imaging) with any a, b or c a. severe narrowing or obliteration of the joint space; or b. severe deformity of the femoral head; or c. all of the following: i. small cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum; and ii. increasing narrowing of the joint space; and iii. moderate loss of sphericity of the femoral head."

The weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph obtained on May 31, 2026 documents joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. This is severe joint-space narrowing accompanied by sclerosis and osteophyte formation, and I ask that it be re-reviewed against the above criteria rather than found insufficient. If Aetna's reviewer applied a different or more specific radiographic threshold (for example, a Tonnis grade determination) that is not visible in the imaging report, I am requesting that the specific finding relied upon be identified in writing so that Dr. Okafor can respond directly to it, including with additional imaging or a formal Tonnis-grade read if needed.

3. Advanced joint disease, pain, and functional impairment

CPB 0287 requires that the "[m]ember has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs) from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the hip joint; and Limited range of motion (ROM), antalgic gait, and pain in hip joint with passive ROM on physical examination."

The record documents 12 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest; ambulation limited to one block and dependent on a cane; and inability to put on shoes unassisted. Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. These findings document pain and functional disability interfering with ADLs and pain with examination of the hip joint, consistent with this element of the Bulletin. [If the examination note does not separately record gait as "antalgic," Dr. Okafor's office can supply an addendum specifically characterizing the gait finding, since the clinical description already on file — cane-assisted ambulation limited to one block — reflects the same functional gait impairment.]

4. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment

CPB 0287 states that members "should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication...), including all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist... ADLs diminished despite completing a plan of care)... and Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications... optional for others); and Therapeutic injections into the hip (required for persons with relative contraindications... optional for others)." The Bulletin defines "relative contraindications" as "morbid obesity (body mass index (BMI) greater than 40), age less than 50 years."

The record documents: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; a corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026 giving only 3 weeks of partial relief; and 20 supervised, in-person physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks (April 21, 2026 through June 30, 2026) targeting hip abductor strengthening and gait, documented in the physical therapy discharge note, with ADLs remaining diminished despite completion of the plan of care. The patient's BMI is 29, which does not meet the Bulletin's "morbid obesity" relative contraindication (BMI greater than 40). [Patient date of birth/age is not stated in the packet provided to me; if the patient is age 50 or older, the applicable conservative-therapy benchmark under the Bulletin is 12 weeks, which the combined NSAID, injection, and physical-therapy course meets or exceeds; if the patient is under 50, the relative-contraindication provisions of the Bulletin apply, and I ask that this be identified so the file can be supplemented accordingly.] The record contains no active infection, no untreated substance use, and no other condition identified in the Bulletin's list of absolute contraindications to total hip replacement.

5. Request

Based on the above, I ask that Aetna reverse the denial of CPT 27130 and authorize the total hip arthroplasty requested by Dr. Okafor. In the alternative, I ask that Aetna identify, in writing, the specific radiographic or clinical element of CPB 0287 (or any other criteria actually applied) that Aetna's reviewer found unmet, including the version and effective date of the criteria used, so that the treating surgeon can respond to that specific finding within the appeal period.

I understand that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the August 14, 2026 notice, i.e., by February 10, 2027, and I am submitting this appeal well within that period. Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the contact information above, with a copy to Dr. Okafor's office at [surgeon's office fax/address/NPI].

Enclosed with this letter:
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 21, 2026 – June 30, 2026, 20 visits)
- Medication and corticosteroid injection records
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and radiology report, May 31, 2026
- Clinic examination note documenting gait, ROM, and provocative testing findings
- [Any additional records the provider elects to include]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Morgan Ellison — signature]
[Date]
